textbookText: 5. What is derived unit?
Ans:- A derived unit is a unit obtained by combining fundamental units according to the laws of physics.
6. How is uniformity of unit checked in an equation?
Ans:- Uniformity is checked by dimensional analysis, where both sides of the equation must have the same dimensions.
7. Define independent variable.
Ans:- An independent variable is the variable that is changed or controlled by the experimenter to study its effect on the
dependent variable.
8. White the SI unit of amount of substance.
Ans:- The SI unit of amount of substance is mole.
9. Find out the fundamental units involved in the joule(J) . Ans:- 1J=1N⋅m=(kg⋅m/𝑠2)⋅m=kg⋅𝑚2/𝑠2.
So, the fundamental units are kilogram (kg), metre (m), and second (s).
10. Which variable depends upon the value of another variable and cannot be determined directly by the experimenter?
Ans:- The dependent variable depends upon the value of another variable and cannot be determined directly by the
experimenter.

2. Some variables should be controlled while performing an experiment. Why?
Ans:- Controlled variables prevent unwanted influences so the effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable is
measured fairly and reliably so, Some variables should be controlled while performing an experiment.

Ans:- The differences between fundamental unit and derived unit are,

Derived units are combinations of fundamentals via

7. A student is going to study the effect of heat on solubility of sugar, mention the independent and dependent variable in this
study
Ans:- Independent variable: temperature (amount of heat).
Dependent variable: solubility of sugar.
